evidence: UNVERIFIED: Kedungu (Kec. Kediri, Tabanan) is a black volcanic sand surf beach but no source found describing swimming; Pantai Nyanyi explicitly not recommended for swimming - https://bali-home-immo.com/id/blog/destinasi-wisata-bali/menikmati-momen-tenang-dengan-berkuda-di-pantai-kedungu

Pantai Mutun (Padang Cermin, Pesawaran) has soft white sand, calm shallow water; waves not too big, suitable for swimming - https://www.detik.com/sumbagsel/wisata/d-8155865/7-wisata-di-pesawaran-yang-jangan-dilewatkan-wajib-dikunjungi

Tambakrejo (Kab. Blitar) white sand, calm waves, described as safe for small children; caveat: Orami says not recommended for swimming (sources conflict) - https://mamikos.com/kost/kost-500k-blitar-murah

Pantai Pelang (Kec. Panggul, Trenggalek) brownish-white sand with a designated swimming area; caveat: big south-coast waves - https://www.detik.com/jatim/wisata/d-8074465/pantai-pelang-trenggalek-surga-tersembunyi-di-pesisir-selatan-jawa-timur

Teluk Kiluan (Tanggamus) gently sloping white-sand beaches with clear water, popular for snorkeling; caveat: no explicit swimming statement, and drownings reported at Pekon Terbaya - https://auto2000.co.id/berita-dan-tips/pantai-di-lampung-tips

Pantai Widuri: fine black sand, calm waves, gentle slope so children can play in the water; caveat: detik says waves are big, and erosion reported - https://www.idxchannel.com/milenomic/deretan-wisata-di-pemalang-yang-lagi-hits-wajib-dikunjungi/all

Pantai Wonokerto (Kab. Pekalongan, Java Sea) visitors play on the sand and swim; caveat: abrasion - https://www.rctiplus.com/news/detail/inews/5382974/libur-panjang--pantai-wonokerto-pekalongan-dipadati-ribuan-wisatawan

Pantai Bandengan (Tirto Samudro, ~7 km north of Jepara) white sand, clear water, small waves suitable for swimming; rainy-season waves can be dangerous - https://www.metrotvnews.com/read/NOlCAe7a-4-pantai-indah-yang-wajib-dikunjungi-saat-ke-jepara

Almost all beaches in the area have ocean currents and big waves; bathing is advised against (no Gianyar beach found described as swimmable) - https://voinews.id/index.php/component/k2/item/21335-purnama-beach-bali

UNVERIFIED: Pantai Permata is eruption-sand flat being replanted with mangrove; no source on swimming (swimmable Bahak/Gili Ketapang are in Kabupaten Probolinggo) - https://mongabay.co.id/2023/07/02/sesalkan-penebangan-mangrove-di-pantai-permata-probolinggo/

Labuhan Jukung (Krui, Pesisir Barat) waves fairly friendly so visitors are allowed to bathe; Tanjung Setia is white sand but surf-only - https://mojok.co/terminal/pesisir-barat-mutiara-di-pojok-tanah-sumatera/

Pantai Barat waves relatively calm and suitable for swimming, child float rental; caveat: swim only in flagged safe zone, rip currents - https://www.indonesia.travel/id/id/travel-ideas/marine/pantai-pangandaran/
Pantai Candikusuma (Melaya, Jembrana) black sand; waters good for swimming and bathing; Medewi is a surf break - https://direktoripariwisata.id/pdf/2922
Pantai Sadranan white sand; offshore rocks hold back waves so at times swimming/snorkeling is safe; caveat: depends on tide/swell - https://ejournal3.undip.ac.id/index.php/jmr/article/view/25903
UNVERIFIED: Morosari (Sayung, Demak) suffers annual abrasion and tidal flooding; no source on sand or swimming - https://ejournal3.undip.ac.id/index.php/jkts/article/view/18721

Police ask tourists not to bathe in the sea from Pantai Trisik to Congot and at Glagah due to strong waves/currents - https://www.inews.id/regional/yogya/antisipasi-kecelakaan-laut-wisatawan-diminta-tak-mandi-di-pantai-trisik-hingga-congot
Blue Lagoon near Padangbai: ~60 m white sand, calm waves, swimming best at higher tide, snorkel from shore - https://hotels.com/go/indonesia/blue-lagoon-beach

Pantai Pandan (Kec. Pandan, Tapteng) fine white sand; swimming and snorkeling, calm waves safe for children - https://www.goodnewsfromindonesia.id/2024/08/12/pantai-pandan-di-tapteng-pasir-putihnya-membuat-wisatawan-ingin-kembali
UNVERIFIED: Pantai Imbo (Lawanga, Poso) is a favourite beach but affected by abrasion; no source on sand type or swimming - https://repository.unsimar.ac.id/1328/4/BAB%20I.pdf
UNVERIFIED: Kapoposang islands have white sandy beaches and coral reefs (dive sites), but no source found describing swimming - https://journal.ipb.ac.id/index.php/jpsp/article/view/4195
